name: Fahmi Fadzil
_note: M2 cohort: federal cabinet minister, in cabinet since 3 Dec 2022 (Communications and Digital, then Communications from the Dec 2023 split). Data on file; below ranking validity pending further objective dimensions and the Layer B panel. Layer B (Editorial Panel) added 2026-06-01 as a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: No corruption charge or conviction of record. A review of court and anti-corruption records to the source date found no personal matter against the minister. Recorded as the subject's own factual status only.

metrics.justification: Response to a nationwide internet-quality crisis: after widespread complaints on 13 Apr 2025 he gave telcos a same-day deadline to submit remediation plans or face MCMC enforcement under the amended Communications and Multimedia Act, contacting the regulator directly. A decisive directive on a discrete service crisis, but the problem recurred in 2026, so the resolution was not durable (anchor 2).

citation.title: Fahmi to telcos: Fix internet issues by 5pm or face MCMC crackdown

metrics.justification: Flagship press reform delivered: the Malaysian Media Council Act passed the Dewan Rakyat 26 Feb 2025 and was gazetted 13 Jun 2025, creating an industry-led self-regulatory body; the social-media licensing framework took effect 1 Jan 2025 with partial platform uptake. Major reform delivered, others partial (anchor 3).

citation.title: Malaysia: Media council bill passed in lower house

metrics.justification: Mixed institutional record: establishing the Malaysian Media Council (gazetted 13 Jun 2025) strengthened a press institution, but civil-society bodies (ARTICLE 19, CIJ, Lawyers for Liberty) formally objected that the Dec 2024 Communications and Multimedia Act s.233 amendments widened state content powers. Building and erosion both documented (anchor 2).

citation.title: Malaysia: Halt the repressive amendments to the Communications and Multimedia Act

metrics.justification: Reversed an earlier 'no age-limit law' stance for social media (stated 8 Dec 2024) when Cabinet discussed raising the minimum registration age to 16 (announced 17 Oct 2025). A documented reversal; an on-record acknowledgement of the shift was not located (anchor 2).

citation.title: Fahmi: No age limit law for social media users, but Malaysia will regulate platforms via licensing
